archetypes.name: kv-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan specifies six emitted KV keys across two extraction targets; any name drift or silent-abort gap between the script spec, the SKILL.md parse block, the test matrix, and the .md documentation breaks orchestrator branches without a compile-time signal.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every KV key emitted by the new subcommands and wrapper (CLEARED, SEEDED, SEED_MODE, EMIT_BODY, WFR_RC, STEP17_EMITTED_PRESENT) for consistency across four surfaces: the per-subcommand emit spec, the SKILL.md parse/branch spec, the test-case assertions, and the .md contract docs. For each failure path (absent file, malformed file, symlink guard, operational I/O failure, set -e abort), verify the plan guarantees the promised KV key is emitted before exit and that no SKILL.md branch can observe a missing key. Check whether existing subcommands in stall-recovery-report.sh emit overlapping key names that could corrupt a downstream parse. Verify that STEP17_EMITTED_PRESENT is either used by the SKILL.md orchestrator spec or explicitly documented as informational-only; if neither, flag the gap. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: helper-path-surface
archetypes.rationale: The plan references at least six helper scripts and in-script functions (atomic_write_text, kv_get, read-session-env-key.sh, write-final-report.sh, append-tool-failure.sh, lib-quiet.sh) that are absent from scope-files.txt; if any are missing, renamed, or at the wrong relative path the extraction fails at runtime with no build-time signal.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/implement/scripts/stall-recovery-report.sh and confirm that atomic_write_text, kv_get, and the sanitizer functions the plan says to reuse actually exist there with compatible signatures. Locate read-session-env-key.sh and append-tool-failure.sh in the repo and verify whether step-18b-final-report.sh's PLUGIN_ROOT-rooted invocation paths match their actual locations. Confirm that write-final-report.sh lives in skills/implement/scripts/ so the $SCRIPT_DIR-rooted call in step-18b-final-report.sh resolves correctly, and check that token-report.sh accepts the --full --format json --output flags the plan specifies. Verify that lib-quiet.sh is reachable at $PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib-quiet.sh from the new wrapper's perspective and exposes the emit/emit_kv API the plan depends on. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-repin
archetypes.rationale: The plan removes specific pin strings from test-implement-structure.sh and test-render-cost-line-callsites.sh; if those strings do not match what currently exists, make lint will either pass silently on the old shape or fail on the new shape, masking the extraction entirely.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/test-implement-structure.sh around the Step 18 assertion block and verify that the exact strings the plan says to remove (_wfr_args+=(--print-stdout), cmp -s within the step:18 region) actually appear there today. Read scripts/test-render-cost-line-callsites.sh and confirm that _wfr_emit_body, inline _wfr_args, and the sed block extracting the old _wfr_args fence exist before removal is safe. Check whether any test files outside scope-files.txt currently pin the old Step-18b Bash shape (--print-stdout, _wfr_args, _wfr_emit_body) and would become stale after the extraction without being listed in the plan. Verify the plan's new pins (step-18b-final-report.sh invocation, EMIT_BODY parse, absence of --print-stdout on any Step-18 write-final-report.sh call) are specific enough to detect a regression if the wrapper path or key name drifts. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
